summary.oneLiner: Aarti Drugs transitioned from investment to operational scale-up in FY26, with Q4 showing sharp sequential recovery (EBITDA +72% QoQ) driven by methylamine plant ramp-up and formulation exports, though PAT declined 12% YoY due to one-off ramp-up costs and input inflation. The thesis hinges on achieving 70%+ utilization in backward-integrated facilities to structurally lower metformin costs and expand margins to 14% in FY27 despite geopolitical crude volatility.

one-line thesis: Aarti Drugs transitioned from investment to operational scale-up in FY26, with Q4 showing sharp sequential recovery (EBITDA +72% QoQ) driven by methylamine plant ramp-up and formulation exports, though PAT declined 12% YoY due to one-off ramp-up costs and input inflation. The thesis hinges on achieving 70%+ utilization in backward-integrated facilities to structurally lower metformin costs and expand margins to 14% in FY27 despite geopolitical crude volatility.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 721.1 Cr (+6% YoY, +20% QoQ); EBITDA: INR 96.6 Cr (flat YoY, +72% QoQ), Margin 13.4%; PAT: INR 55.3 Cr (-12% YoY, +36% QoQ), Margin 7.7%; Order Book: Not disclosed (demand visibility via signed contracts for brownfield); Net Debt: ~INR 576 Cr (LT INR 328 Cr + ST INR 248 Cr), D/E at historic lows. One-offs: INR 18-20 Cr EBITDA loss from new project ramp-ups (Sayakha/Salicylic) in FY26; temporary shutdown of Salicylic acid due to variable losses.
guidance: Revenue Growth: 8-10% volume growth targeted (internal target 10-15%); Margin: 13.5-14.0% EBITDA for FY27 (vs 13.4% in Q4); Order Inflow: Strong visibility in regulated markets (US/EU) with 12-18 month flow timeline; Capex: INR 300-400 Cr over next 2-3 years (quasi-greenfield/brownfield).
order book & pipeline: No specific backlog value disclosed; growth backed by signed contracts for existing products and late-stage dossier approvals (oncology/non-oncology) in regulated markets.
segment / subsidiary detail: APIs: Antibiotics (37.8% of sales), Anti-protozoal (19.6%), Antidiabetic (15.0%), Anti-inflammatory (11.9%), Anti-fungal (10.0%). Domestic revenue +7% YoY, Exports -7% YoY. Formulations: Revenue INR 91.3 Cr (+41% YoY), 69% from exports; FY26 total INR 330.5 Cr (+16% YoY). Regulated market contribution rose to 73% of exports.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Backward integration in Metformin (methylamines) reducing China dependence; 2) US FDA approval pending for Metformin facility; 3) Oncology formulation plant (pre-revenue) with dossier filings; 4) Salicylic acid derivatives plant commissioning (May/June 2026) with higher margin profile.
margins & cost dynamics: Q4 Gross Margin improved sequentially; Manufacturing costs expected to reduce by ~1% aiding EBITDA. FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 13.5-14.0% (100-200 bps improvement potential). Headwinds: Elevated crude/gas costs impacting antibiotic demand elasticity if prices exceed $110-120/barrel.
capex / expansion: INR 300-400 Cr planned over 2-3 years for brownfield expansions (OSD block, Metformin capacity) and oncology R&D. CWIP stands at INR 214 Cr (cogen boiler, formulation R&D, oncology dossiers).
capital allocation: Debt reduction prioritized (D/E at historic lows); Capex funded via internal accruals and existing debt headroom; No dividend specifics mentioned, focus on reinvestment for margin expansion.
risks & watch-items: 1) Geopolitical: West Asia war extending crude >$120/barrel suppressing domestic antibiotic volumes; 2) Execution: Delays in Salicylic acid equipment installation and effluent cost competitiveness vs China; 3) Regulatory: Timing of US FDA inspections for Metformin/Oncology; 4) Input Cost: Ammonia supply constraints.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'execution year' completion, sequential recovery, and structural cost benefits from integration. Acknowledges external volatility (war) but confident in volume growth and margin repair by FY27.
non-obvious takeaways: Salicylic acid was voluntarily shut down in Q4 due to variable losses pending phenol recovery equipment installation; Management explicitly links antibiotic volume risk to crude price elasticity in the domestic regulated market (NLEM impact).
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| High crude prices inflating API costs but benefiting integrated players with fixed-cost advantages | Aarti Drugs Ltd | beneficiary | High | Backward integration in methylamines/metformin provides cost arbitrage vs peers dependent on Chinese imports; FY27 margin expansion guided despite macro headwinds. |
| Salicylic acid margin pressure from Chinese effluent dumping and lack of phenol recovery | Generic Salicylic Acid Peers | loser | Med | Aarti's temporary shutdown highlights sector-wide margin compression; only players with antidumping protection or derivative integration will survive. |

themes.title: Pharma US complex-generics & specialty exports
themes.need: US complex generics, Para-IV FTFs and the GLP-1/semaglutide wave still drive export pharma, but Q1FY27 delivered one hard setback and one deliberate trough. DRREDDY held an out-of-cycle call disclosing a semaglutide injectable API scale-up validation failure - an out-of-spec impurity in finished product - halting supply through roughly September and re-cutting FY27 volumes to 6-7 million pens (Q3-Q4) from an earlier ~12mn first-year target, which re-times India's largest semaglutide launch and opens a share window for rivals. CIPLA let EBITDA margin fall to 16.7%, below the pre-Revlimid level, because launch opex is committed ahead of revenue plus ~1-2% of revenue in war-related input cost - yet reaffirmed BOTH an FY27 18.5-20% margin and a $1bn US exit run-rate off a $162m Q1, making this a trough by design with unusually large operating leverage if the launches land. The GLP-1 opportunity is bifurcating: CIPLA's Yurpeak (tirzepatide, Eli Lilly collaboration) did INR 80cr and is already the #2 anti-obesity brand behind Mounjaro while Cipla deliberately sits out the crowded semaglutide-generic price war. NATCOPHARM remains in a gRevlimid post-cliff base year; LUPIN/ALKEM/ZYDUSLIFE/LAURUSLABS carry cleaner momentum; SENORES/MARKSANS on US generics; DIVISLAB on GLP-1 peptides (55% CDMO mix).
themes.driver: DRREDDY's semaglutide supply restart (guided ~September) and whether the 6-7mn-pen re-cut holds; CIPLA's four US launches landing against the reaffirmed 18.5-20% FY27 margin; FTF launches and USFDA clearances; DIVISLAB Kakinada Unit 3 from FY27.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.
